decision.summary: The Federal Reserve voted to keep its target interest rate at 0 to 1/4 percent.

changes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in September indicates that economic growth strengthened somewhat in the third quarter, reflecting in part a reversal of the temporary factors that had weighed on growth earlier in the year.
changes.explanation: The Fed noted that third-quarter economic growth picked up because some temporary problems faded away.

changes.quote: Household spending has increased at a somewhat faster pace in recent months.
changes.explanation: Consumer spending showed signs of improvement compared to previous months.

changes.quote: Business investment in equipment and software has continued to expand, but investment in nonresidential structures is still weak, and the housing sector remains depressed.
changes.explanation: While companies continue to buy equipment and software, the commercial building and housing markets remain weak.

changes.quote: The Committee continues to expect a moderate pace of economic growth over coming quarters and consequently anticipates that the unemployment rate will decline only gradually toward levels that the Committee judges to be consistent with its dual mandate.
changes.explanation: The Fed expects slow and steady growth, meaning the unemployment rate will fall only very gradually.

changes.quote: To support a stronger economic recovery and to help ensure that inflation, over time, is at levels consistent with the dual mandate, the Committee decided today to continue its program to extend the average maturity of its holdings of securities as announced in September.
changes.explanation: The Fed is continuing its ongoing program to twist the maturity of its bond holdings to support the recovery.

tone_quotes.quote: Nonetheless, recent indicators point to continuing weakness in overall labor market conditions, and the unemployment rate remains elevated.
Moreover, there are significant downside risks to the economic outlook, including strains in global financial markets.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 12.89% APR costs about $53.71 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 2.03% and moved +2 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 4.11% would rise by about $3.48 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 9%, and employers added an average of 138k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 3.8% over the past year (September 2011); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.9%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a -0.1% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved 0 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.54% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that the Fed intends to keep interest rates exceptionally low at least through mid-2013.

citations.detail: The Committee also decided to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent
